basis: Glycogen metabolic defects; hepatic involvement in roughly 60-80% and myopathy in roughly 30-40% across common forms. Cardiac damage is subtype-dependent.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic glycogenoses constitute most patients, roughly 60-80%, with impaired hepatic glycogen handling.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: muscle disease across types II, III and V affects approximately 30-40% overall; frequency varies by subtype.

basis: Craniosynostosis and nasolacrimal duct agenesis are characteristic structural malformations; the lacrimal system belongs to ocular.

decisions.ocular: primary: nasolacrimal duct agenesis is a defining malformation of the lacrimal drainage system.

basis: Definition includes skeletal, skin and CNS overgrowth; vascular malformations occur in 80-99%. Ear-canal exostoses (30-79%) omitted at cap; lung lobation alone adds no axis.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the supplied definition explicitly includes central nervous system overgrowth among the defining affected tissues.

basis: Complex cardiac malformations and congenital asplenia define the syndrome; asplenia (5/5) removes splenic blood and immune functions. Organ position and lung lobation add no axis.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: defining congenital asplenia causes an intrinsic deficiency of splenic immune function; this is not merely a later infection risk.

basis: ACTH-driven cortisol excess causes muscle wasting/bone loss in roughly 50-80% and persistent dermal atrophy/easy bruising in over 50%; hypertension is separately diagnosed.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic cortisol excess directly causes dermal atrophy, fragility and striae; characteristic skin damage affects over 50%.

basis: Gonadal, cardiac and renal defects define syndrome; ear-canal atresia 80-99%. Cap omits mild developmental impairment and skeletal defects (80-99%), clefts (30-79%) and scalp defects.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac malformations are part of the syndrome's definition; VSD is annotated in 80-99%.
decisions.renal: primary: renal malformations are part of the definition; ureter defects occur in 80-99% and renal hypoplasia/aplasia in 30-79%.
decisions.neurologic: none at cap: mild intellectual disability/developmental delay occurs in 80-99%; severe structural cardiac, renal and ear defects take priority.
decisions.otologic: involved: external auditory canal atresia occurs in 80-99%, directly compromising the conductive hearing apparatus.

basis: Usually apical lung malignancy with defining brachial plexus and vessel compression; direct invasion of thoracic bones is usual over the course (>30%).

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the supplied definition includes thoracic-outlet vessel obstruction/compression, with impaired drainage and extremity edema.

basis: The synonym chondroid syringoma identifies a cutaneous sweat-gland mixed tumor; its vulvar location does not exclude a skin-adnexal origin.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: chondroid syringoma denotes a skin-adnexal sweat-gland tumor; the definition's vulvar location does not contradict that origin.

basis: Malignancy originates in exocrine pancreatic ducts. Hepatic metastases are separately diagnosed secondary cancers; jaundice alone does not establish direct hepatic damage.

decisions.hepatic: none: liver metastases are separately diagnosed secondary malignancies; obstructive jaundice alone does not establish qualifying hepatic tissue damage.

basis: Atypical lymphoid proliferation is a hematologic lesion; this nonspecific concept does not establish lymphoma, immunodeficiency or an immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: atypical lymphoid hyperplasia does not itself establish lymphoma or immune dysfunction; broad immune-disorder ancestry is insufficient.
